faq.a: Yahya is associated with the Arabic form يَحْيَى, whose core sense is yahya; john (prophet); he lives.

faq.q: What is the origin of Yahya?
faq.a: Yahya is associated with Arabic. Yahya is Arabic يَحْيَى (Yaḥyā), the Quranic form of the prophet John, associated with the sense 'he lives'.
Yes — the underlying form يَحْيَى is Arabic.
Yahya can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Yahya should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Yaḥyā is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet John and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Yahya mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Yahya is rendered یحیی and carries the sense یحیی، زنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ya-hya. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Yahya, yahya. Script forms are يَحْيَى, یحیی, یحییٰ, यहया.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
